chapter: Union career, Masons, mentoring and the Clef Club
title: Schooling and becoming a Past Master Mason
summary: Howard says the union job pushed him to study, which led to becoming a Past Master of his Masonic lodge.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Oh, boy, she played the devil out of a piano. Make you sick with a piano. And then when I got working for the union, when I got that job up there at the union, and they told me I had to go to school. And I went to school and studied. But I didn't think it was going to be that long. I didn't think it was going to take me around like it's done now, and the things that I have
Anybody has to tell me to go. (Inaudible).

accomplished since then, and there have been lots and lots of things that I've accomplished. And I was working out there -- did Marshall Royal tell you about it? He was working down the street from me. Let me show you something here.
It was the greatest thing that ever happened to me.
Yes. You want to tell us something about your Masonic experience?

Sure. All I can say is after years of studying and practicing I made the -- oh, I can't think what you call it. Now, let's see here, if I can get it together. Oh, no, I can't find it here. It's hard for me to find. But I made the -- from that job up there that I took --
For the union. I studied and got straightened out till I'm a Past Master of the Lodge.
I think you said Grand Master, didn't you?

Yeah not Grand Master. Past Master. I was (unintelligible) Master of the Lodge that I belonged to, and then a past Master of the Lodge, and I got the Grand -- what do they call this? Okay, excuse me. I got the Grand Order from the Grand Master.
Mr. Collette: In so many different fields.
Oh, yeah, I've been going a long time.
I can't remember all the things, Buddy. I wish somebody could take this out, out of my mouth and out of my heart and my mind, and tell you about it.
You're telling us. Just a little closer.
I do wish somebody could take it out of my heart and out of my mind and bring it to somebody who could take it and tell them what it's all about. I don't know. I can't tell people. Never could.
